clue.text: What to eat in historic town (Earl's)?

definitions.text: What to eat in historic town (Earl's)?

parts.words: What to eat in historic town (Earl's)?
parts.note: the food named after the Earl who took his title from a historic town in Kent, read as both the snacks and the town's possessions

explanation.surface: A tourist asks what food to try when visiting an old town.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a historic town in Kent; the fourth Earl of Sandwich is said to have asked for meat between bread slices so he could keep gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread with fillings is named after the Earl whose title came from the Kent town.

clue.text: Tender doctor turned up in case

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters inside the word for a case

parts.note: a case in law is a suit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor turns up in court with a case and makes an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' signals reading upwards, which suits a down light; 'Tender' is the verb, not the adjective about soreness.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something, such as a proposal, is to submit or put it forward formally.

clue.text: Head will, it's said, settle comfortably

indicators.note: it's said tells us the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a head is a headland or NESS, and will is shortened to 'll, so the phrase says Ness'll

explanation.surface: A head of the family declares he will settle down comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: A NESS is a headland (Loch Ness aside, the word appears in place names like Sheerness); NESS'LL spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle down and settle cosily into a place.

clue.text: Sequential artist might allow hair to be styled

indicators.note: hair to be styled suggests rearranging, so the letters of the preceding words are reworked

explanation.surface: An artist who works in series might let a hairdresser style him.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogarth, the 18th-century English painter, made picture series such as A Rake's Progress, hence 'Sequential'.
explanation.definitionFit: The English painter produced narrative series of pictures to be viewed in order, like a comic strip.

clue.text: Foreign gent's strange role in support of conspiracy

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece in support of another sits below it

parts.note: a cabal is a secret plotting group, a conspiracy

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man abroad plays an odd part in a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' gives LERO; 'in support of' works because in a down light the lower piece holds up the upper one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish gentleman or horseman is called a caballero, a foreign term for a gent.

clue.text: He, reportedly, is behind energy message

indicators.note: behind places the second piece after the first

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: reportedly means a word heard said, not spelt

parts.note: he refers to a male

explanation.surface: Someone claims a man is behind an energy message.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE heard aloud gives MAIL, placed after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a message sent over a computer network.

clue.text: Mark's causing alarm no end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: something causing alarm is frightening or scary

explanation.surface: A mark is causing great alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' looks like 'endlessly', intensifying the alarm; here it trims the last letter of SCARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Innocence of children, Italian, evident during stay abroad

indicators.note: during places one piece inside another, with 'evident' joining
abroad suggests going astray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: Children and an Italian show innocence while staying overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' gives ASTY; 'during' signals the insertion, with 'evident' only a joining word meaning showing up there.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastity is sexual purity, a form of innocence.

clue.text: Revolutionary annoyed relief organisation

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
annoyed means cross

explanation.surface: An angry revolutionary heads a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The international humanitarian movement gives medical and disaster relief.

clue.text: Like a measure army officer adopted in most cases

indicators.note: adopted means the officer is taken inside the phrase

parts.note: like means as
a rule is a measuring stick
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: An army officer adopts a measure that applies in most cases.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or generally, true in most instances.

clue.text: Lecturer leaving Essex town plant

indicators.note: leaving means the lecturer is taken out of the town

parts.note: Basildon is a town in Essex, a county east of London
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A lecturer departs from an Essex town where the plant is.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb, a plant used in cooking.

clue.text: Group of musicians producing money belt

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a band is a strip such as a belt

explanation.surface: Musicians produce a money belt.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble of trumpets, cornets and tubas is a band of musicians.

clue.text: What adverse decision may result in?

definitions.text: What adverse decision may result in?

parts.words: What adverse decision may result in?
parts.note: a decision is a will, and an adverse one is a bad will, which leads to resentment

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a ruling against them could lead to.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'will' as a decision, as in free will; an adverse will is ill will, which also means hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or resentment can follow an unfavourable ruling.

clue.text: Barge's means of ignition

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed boat used to unload ships is a barge
a device that produces a flame to light cigarettes

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat barge for unloading ships and a device for lighting cigarettes share this name.

clue.text: Praise Monet's remarkable apes

indicators.note: remarkable means extraordinary, suggesting the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S counted as letters

explanation.surface: Praise for Monet's remarkable apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apes' looks like a noun about monkeys in a painting; it is the verb meaning copies.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or copy them, as an impersonator does.

clue.text: Sailor's pique concerning compound

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
a pet is a fit of sulking, a pique
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A sailor's irritation concerns a compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Notice Conservative has thrown money down

parts.note: to notice is to spot

indicators.note: thrown means the word is tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices a Tory throwing cash about.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made immediately on delivery is money paid down.

clue.text: Film celebrities touring Warwickshire

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: celebrities are stars
WAR is an abbreviation for Warwickshire, an English Midlands county

explanation.surface: Famous people are on a tour of Warwickshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The science-fiction saga begun by George Lucas in 1977 is a film.

clue.text: Well-earned revenue?

parts.note: money earned from oil wells, not money deserved

explanation.surface: A deserved income is praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollars earned by oil-exporting countries come from their oil wells.

clue.text: A current at sea

parts.note: a drift is a flow or current

explanation.surface: A current out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea in the sense of lost or confused is to be adrift.

clue.text: Ready to drive off from home with household stuff

parts.note: in means at home
gear means belongings, stuff

explanation.surface: Ready to drive away from home with the household belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: A car in gear is engaged and ready to move off.

clue.text: To our sailors, trouble is a violent windstorm

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, British sailors
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: For British sailors a violent storm is trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violently rotating column of wind.

clue.text: Last letter from home (Gateshead)

indicators.note: from shows the answer is drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The final letter arrives from home in Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town on the Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet is omega.

clue.text: Hurt fencing juvenile champion

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: hurt means pain
a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A young fencing champion is hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin is a knightly champion, one of Charlemagne's peers.

clue.text: Set of rooms beside Thames originally housing soldiers

indicators.note: housing means the soldiers are placed inside

parts.note: apart can mean aside or beside, separate

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter is used

parts.note: men are soldiers

explanation.surface: Rooms by the Thames house soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' signals the container; 'beside' as APART is the sense of aside or separate from.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms for living in.

clue.text: Make one marry

definitions.meaning: to combine things into a single whole
to join together, as in matrimony

explanation.definitionFit: To join is to combine into a single whole, and also to wed.

clue.text: Chop up hard wood

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
ash is a wood

explanation.surface: Chop up hard wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To hash food is to chop it into small pieces.

clue.text: Power shown by outstanding dog, early leader in race

parts.note: ace means excellent, outstanding
a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: An outstanding dog shows power as it leads early in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who sets the speed at the front is the early leader.
